course_description:
How do you turn ideas into real-world impact? In this capstone, you will bring together everything you’ve learned in Innovation and Entrepreneurship to work directly with industry through a professional placement. You’ll tackle real-world challenges, build networks, and develop the skills to create and scale innovative solutions.

This capstone course is designed to consolidate and apply your learning from across the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Field of Study in a practical, high-impact Work Integrated Learning experience. You will have the opportunity to work in a start-up, with a commercial partner in a technology commercialisation project, or as an entrepreneurship consultant in an incubator or accelerator. These pathways allow you to explore different innovation contexts—commercial, corporate, and social—helping you shape your future career direction.

A key feature of the course is the emphasis on learning through real-world practice. You will engage with ambiguous challenges, test and refine ideas, and contribute to projects with tangible impact. Along the way, you will build capabilities highly valued by employers, including strategic thinking, adaptability, collaboration, and stakeholder communication.

The course is interactive and applied, with a strong focus on self-direction, teamwork, and industry engagement. It also supports your employability by helping you expand your professional networks and gain experience working within innovation-driven environments, both locally and globally.

course_aims: This capstone aims to help you apply and enhance your entrepreneurial mindset for real-world impact through immersive industry engagement. It focuses on developing your ability to navigate uncertainty, create value in practice, and build professional networks with partners, investors, and mentors to support your transition into innovation-driven careers.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse the complexities of founding, investing, and growing a business by applying innovation and entrepreneurship theory.
Develop evidence-based solutions to real-world business model innovation challenges, individually or as a team.
Communicate entrepreneurial insights and ideas to generate stakeholder buy-in and build diverse partnerships.
Reflect on the development of your entrepreneurial mindset, self-efficacy, and social capital.
Conduct primary research through experimentation and/or stakeholder engagement to validate and refine proposed solutions.

assessment_details.due_date: Week 3 Tue - Week 4 Tue Presentations will be scheduled in class time from 5PM during weeks 3 and 4.

assessment_details.task_description: Individual or team (if WIL is based on working with own startup team) presentation of 10 minutes followed by Q&A. Identify and analyse an innovation and/or entrepreneurship issue relevant to your placement: a startup, incubator, accelerator, or business industry partner. The assessment piece must demonstrate thoughtful application of theory to innovation and entrepreneurial, or more specifically, venture creation and growth practice . The main research objective/s or question/s must be related to finding a solution to a practical problem or business model innovation issue encountered during the WIL, placement, or own venture that students want to investigate further by applying existing theories and research. You will therefore do a brief presentation to outline and explain your intended topic, objectives, methodology and/or approach as well as the expected outcomes of your major assignment piece (Report or business case). This will vary in accordance with the nature of the placement that you are undertaking. Please Note: The presentation will be recorded for marking purposes per UQ Policy. assessment_details.title: Reflective Interview (live)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Time limited, Work integrated learning, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: You will sit a single secure in-person interview, framed as a reflective discussion with a potential employer or investor, structured in two parts. In the first part, you will speak to an unscripted set of questions about what you learnt during your placement. In the second part, the interviewer presents a short, unseen case or scenario drawn from the innovation and entrepreneurship domain, and you must apply your placement learning to it live, reasoning aloud about what you would do and why. The discussion remains conversational with the interviewer probing both the reflection and the transfer. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Project report or business case
assessment_details.other_conditions: Peer assessment factor, Work integrated learning. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires you to document and analyse the work you completed during your Work Integrated Learning (WIL) placement. Assessment 3 builds directly on your previous work: Assessment 1 outlined your problem, research questions, and proposed methodology Assessment 2 captured your reflections on your WIL experience. Assessment 3 presents what you actually accomplished, the value you created, and what you learned Your report should be suitable for both academic assessment and your partner startup/organisation (if applicable). Your report should address: Project Context: Briefly revisit your Assessment 1 proposal—the problem you addressed, research questions, and any adjustments made based on feedback Execution & Findings: Document what you actually did—activities, data collection, analysis, and discoveries. Include specific evidence (numbers, quotes, examples) Deliverables & Recommendations: Present tangible outputs and evidence-based recommendations for your partner organisation or venture Theory-Practice Reflection: Critically reflect on how entrepreneurship methodologies influenced your work. Connect to insights from your reflective interviews where relevant Required elements: APA-style references (separate reference list) Professional presentation/format suitable for external stakeholders Tables, figures, or charts may be included to support the discussion Optional appendices for key artefacts (e.g., interview protocols, Business Model Canvas) Read full task description Hide full task description
